name: DIM supplement
lead: 3,3'-Diindolylmethane (DIM) is a compound formed when the body digests indole-3-carbinol, which occurs in cruciferous vegetables such as broccoli, cabbage and Brussels sprouts. It is sold as a dietary supplement [1][2].

In looksmaxxing and acne circles, DIM is promoted as an estrogen-metabolism supplement for hormonal acne. The research identified for this article concerns cancer chemoprevention, hormone metabolism and laboratory biology; no clinical studies of DIM for acne or appearance were found.
infobox: Dietary supplement; indole from cruciferous vegetables

paras: Under acidic conditions such as stomach acid, indole-3-carbinol converts to a series of condensation products, of which DIM is a major component, and these are thought to account for many of its biological effects [3].

Glucosinolate breakdown products from cruciferous vegetables are reported to alter the metabolism and activity of sex hormones in ways that could inhibit hormone-sensitive cancers, although epidemiological evidence for an inverse association with cancer risk is mixed [4]. In laboratory work, DIM showed aryl hydrocarbon receptor-mediated antiestrogenic activity [5]. In vitro, DIM has been reported to inhibit histone deacetylases and to bind weakly to cannabinoid receptors [1].
A mouse study examined the pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution of indole-3-carbinol and its acid condensation products after oral dosing [6].

No studies found for acne or appearance outcomes. Registered human studies of DIM have looked at other conditions, including breast cancer [7][8], prostate cancer [9], thyroid disease [10], lupus [11] and healthy volunteers [12]; several were small, and some were terminated or withdrawn.

The chemical's hazard classification lists skin, eye and respiratory irritation for the pure compound [1]. Long-term safety in people using it for hormonal acne has not been described in studies identified here.

card.summary: Broccoli-derived estrogen-metabolism supplement used for hormonal acne; the research is on cancer and hormones, not skin.
card.note: No acne or appearance trials found; human studies cover other conditions.

quick.overview:
DIM is a compound made from cruciferous vegetables and sold as a supplement. In acne communities it is used with the idea that it shifts estrogen metabolism and calms hormonal breakouts.

No clinical studies of DIM for acne were found; human research has focused on cancer and other conditions.
quick.mechanism: DIM forms from indole-3-carbinol in the stomach. Lab studies report antiestrogenic activity via the aryl hydrocarbon receptor and altered sex hormone metabolism.
quick.risks: Pure DIM carries skin, eye and respiratory irritation hazard labelling. Long-term effects of supplementation for acne have not been studied in the sources reviewed.
